title: Project 4: file-based expense tracker

understand.concept: A file-based expense tracker records date, category and amount, calculates totals and reloads saved entries. It must validate numeric values and handle file-open, read, write and close failures.
understand.whyItMatters: The project applies structures, file streams, parsing and aggregation to a useful persistent-data problem.
understand.analogy: Treat the project or language feature as a set of components with explicit interfaces and responsibilities.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy does not replace C's formal language, library and resource-management rules.

explain.narrative:
A file-based expense tracker records date, category and amount, calculates totals and reloads saved entries. It must validate numeric values and handle file-open, read, write and close failures.

For a complete implementation, define input constraints, ownership, error handling and test cases before coding. Compile with warnings and verify normal, boundary and failure behaviour.

examples.title: Focused C example
examples.explanation: The program appends one record to a text file and checks both the write and close. A full project must define a parseable format and validate every field when reading.

practise.guidedTask: List the fields needed for a useful expense record.
practise.independentTask: Implement add, list and total commands. Test malformed file lines, missing files and failed writes.
hints: Use a documented delimiter and escaping policy for text records.
Do not assume every line in an existing file is valid.
Keep currency representation and rounding policy explicit.
